t: Three Forces, One Stage, then Agam Band
x: Three Forces, One Stage, 6:30 to 7:30 PM: Harish Sivaramakrishnan, Sumanth Manjunath and Banjo Rancho bring together diverse sounds and traditions in a special musical collaboration. Harish Sivaramakrishnan is the lead vocalist and a founder member of the Bengaluru Carnatic progressive rock band Agam, and a playback singer in Malayalam, Tamil and Telugu cinema; in 2021 he won the SIIMA award for Best Playback Singer (Male) in Tamil for "Veyyon Silli" from Soorarai Pottru. Sumanth Manjunath is a violinist from Mysuru and Banjo Rancho is a drummer from Malta. Then Agam Band, 7:30 PM onwards: AGAM, the Carnatic Progressive Rock Experience, an acclaimed Bengaluru band that brings together the richness of Carnatic music and the energy of progressive rock. One ticket includes both shows.

Exploring rhythm, creativity and possibilities of the drum set. An engaging, fun and interactive workshop on the drum set, its history and evolution, and how it is used across musical styles and beyond music, in dance, theatre, film and sound effects. It looks at traditional and contemporary approaches, solo and group playing, composition and improvisation, with practical demonstrations and hands-on work on rhythmic patterns, stick techniques, coordination and practice methods. Open to everyone. No previous experience is necessary.

t: A Kathak Performance, then Khechara Academy of Bharatanatyam
x: 3:30 to 4:30 PM: Internationally touring Kathak dancer Labonee Mohanta will captivate you with lightning-fast spins, intricate footwork, expressive storytelling, and dynamic rhythmic interplay with live musicians. She will also showcase the unique innovation of Kathak Yoga, in which she dances, plays an instrument, and sings, all at the same time! Then 4:30 to 5:45 PM: a Bharatanatyam performance by Anuradha Sridhar and Khechara Academy of Bharatanatyam, Bengaluru. One ticket includes both shows.

t: Dance Alchemy, then Sri Nimishambha School of Dance
x: 5:45 to 6:20 PM: Experience Dance Alchemy, a first-of-its-kind celebration of movement, bringing together Western dance styles, Indian classical forms, folk traditions and cultural influences. Curated by globally acclaimed Latin dance exponent Lourd Vijay, this unique production promises an exciting fusion of rhythms and styles. Then 6:20 to 7:35 PM: Sri Nimishambha School of Dance, curated by Apthamitra-fame Guru Vidwan Sridhar Jain, presenting a vibrant showcase of Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi and Indian folk, beautifully interwoven with elements of fusion. One ticket includes both shows.

Discover the art of linocut printmaking in this hands-on creative workshop. Drawing inspiration from classical Indian dance mudras, rhythmic percussion patterns and traditional temple architecture, participants will sketch, carve and print their own unique designs. Learn basic carving techniques, explore textures and patterns, and create beautiful handmade prints on cotton rag paper to take home. No prior printmaking experience required.
Age: 18+
Duration: 2.5 hours
Prerequisites: None

t: The Warrior's Path, then Mahabharata: A Mirror to Humanity
x: 7:00 PM: The Making of an Epic Warrior. A Kalaripayattu performance by Atha Beyond that imagines how a warrior of the Mahabharata age would have trained, in body, mind and spirit: surrender to the guru, forging the body, one-pointed focus, mastery of weapons, and the warrior's code of knowing when not to strike. Told through authentic Kalari practice, with an oil lamp, live percussion and moments of silence. It continues straight into Mahabharata: A Mirror to Humanity, with no break. A captivating theatrical dance and movement experience exploring the untold stories, emotions and complexities of Ambe, Karna, Draupadi, Bheema and Duryodhana. Vyjayanthi Kashi as Ambe, Mallika Sarabhai as Draupadi, Dr. Lakshminarayan as Karna and Dr. Vasanth Kiran as Bheema bring the timeless epic to life through powerful storytelling and dance. One ticket includes both shows.
